title: Prove the sharp width-two paid-history threshold for bit-flip targets
body:
This scoped proof gives the exact standalone paid-return threshold for the bit-flip family h=aI+bX. Width one permits zero paid returns; every width at least two requires one return per distinct independent target owner. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged.

[Proof and scope](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/616bf049b669d56a2bf21de130941f8de3f5d7bf/research/flip-history-sharp-width/README.md), [exact checks](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/616bf049b669d56a2bf21de130941f8de3f5d7bf/research/flip-history-sharp-width/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/616bf049b669d56a2bf21de130941f8de3f5d7bf/research/flip-history-sharp-width/SOURCES.json), [registered replay](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/616bf049b669d56a2bf21de130941f8de3f5d7bf/research/flip-history-sharp-width/VERIFY.json). Base: canonical main `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`, priority revision 7. Contribution head: `616bf049b669d56a2bf21de130941f8de3f5d7bf`.

The field has characteristic different from two, ab(a squared minus b squared) is nonzero, and ordinary operators are the span of I and the simultaneous bit flip. Initial observations are ordinary only. Arbitrary finite feedback, overwrite and width-dependent scalar choices are allowed. The upper count is attained if each target lift is an available paid primitive. Cached nonordinary observations and physical caller charges are outside scope.

CPython 3.12.14 registered normal and optimized checks pass: 28 parameter pairs, 140 literal Gaussian-rational tensor matrices, 336 complete owner-block cases, 1764 character identities and 13 boundary controls. Both modes print `PASS_FLIP_HISTORY_SHARP_WIDTH`; the launcher prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The one-dimensional character distinguishes targets already at width two, although the full coset spans can still intersect there.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/flip-history-sharp-width
```

Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice. Committed-byte checks pass. No selected cold replay, native compiler, Lean, Docker, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. The proof is not a source-bound physical supplier or an all-group cutoff improvement. Hosted status is unconfirmed at publication.

Credit Chris R (@Clear1nsight) and the retained [PR #5425](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5425) and [PR #5446](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5446) authors for the actual-return history method and smaller-width question. The [exact pointwise proof and square-root-of-X example](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0d0bcf3fa261c9591e7e60ed5926c6e04d360f9e/docs/research/standalone-history-scalar-ceiling/proofs/pointwise-lemma-v1.md) are the direct precedents. Classical involution characters and tensor eigenvectors retain their credit. The [scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19169154) excludes the physical-history work in [PR #5447](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5447).

Next: compute a detecting character component for one specified larger ordinary group and bind it to a physical source. Its initial observation and ownership ledger remains necessary.

Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
